title: Using AI to decode language from the brain and advance our understanding of human communication
summary: A deep-learning decoder translated non-invasive EEG and MEG signals recorded during typing into sentence characters in an offline demonstration with 35 healthy volunteers. Mean character error rates were 67% for EEG and 32% for MEG, with a best MEG result of 19%. Participants typed memorized sentences; the work does not establish unrestricted or real-time communication.
ai_technology: A deep-learning decoder maps non-invasive EEG/MEG signals recorded during typing to sentence characters.

source_review.scope: Official Meta announcement and linked primary Brain-to-Text preprint abstract and full text; first preprint version checked.

evidence.tested: The primary preprint evaluated 35 healthy volunteers; mean character error rates were 67% for EEG and 32% for MEG, with best MEG 19%.
evidence.unknown: Healthy skilled typists, memorized text, offline decoding and shielded-room MEG limit generalization; distinct from invasive handwriting BCI.
